messages:
Maya: FYI escalation from a customer — they lost decrypt audit logs during a KMS HSM failover window and are hitting AccessDenied on decrypts. Customer says this affects billing reconciliation (missing decrypt events). Can someone triage?

Jamal: Can you paste the KMS key ARN and a snippet of the error the customer is seeing? Also which region and account?

Maya: Key ARN: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:210987654321:key/9f8e7d6c-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-1234567890ab
Customer account: 210987654321 (partner account).
Error from their logs: `AccessDeniedException: not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:210987654321:key/9f8e7d6c-...`
They also ran a CloudTrail lookup and say decrypt events for ~2028-12-02 02:10-02:25 UTC are missing from the S3 audit bucket.

Kai: Two quick possibilities: 1) decrypts actually succeeded but encryptionContext mismatch prevents us from correlating events, 2) CloudTrail delivery lag or S3 lifecycle/archive removed those specific objects, 3) cross-account grants or key policy denies. Did they use an encryption context at encrypt time?

Maya: Customer says their producer sets `{"job":"billing-ingest","tenant":"acct-123"}` as encryption context. Consumer app logs show decrypt attempts with only `{"job":"billing-ingest"}` (tenant missing). They think HSM failover coincided with a redeploy where env var for tenant got lost.

Sara: That matches the billing reconciliation issue — if decrypt calls are failing intermittently then our pipeline emitted partial success records and billing reconciler can't tie tokens back to owners. We need to confirm whether those decrypts were actually attempted (CloudTrail PutEvents) or if they never reached KMS because of network/failover routing.

oncall-bot: Scheduled maintenance: KMS-HSM-cluster-usc-east-1 failover test at 2028-12-02T02:05Z — duration ~20m (ops). See incident: https://infra.company/internal/ops/789

Alex: Repro steps I'd try locally (partner account impersonation via STS):
1) encrypt using `aws kms encrypt --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:210987654321:key/9f8e7d6c-... --plaintext fileb://payload.bin --encryption-context '{"job":"billing-ingest","tenant":"acct-123"}' --output text --query CiphertextBlob > ct.b64`
2) decode `echo ct.b64 | base64 --decode > ct.bin`
3) attempt decrypt with missing context: `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --encryption-context '{"job":"billing-ingest"}' --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:210987654321:key/9f8e7d6c-...'`
You should see `AccessDeniedException` if contexts differ. If decrypt succeeds then the issue is likely CloudTrail or policy.

Jamal: Also run `aws kms list-grants --key-id <key>` and `aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <key>` and `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <key> --policy-name default` in the partner account (or with a role from partner account) to check for cross-account grants.

Maya: I asked the customer to run the decrypt repro above and send back the exact CLI output and the CloudTrail lookup command they used: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:210987654321:key/9f8e7d6c-... --start-time 2028-12-02T02:00:00Z --end-time 2028-12-02T02:30:00Z`

Customer (paste): "we ran the decrypt repro — missing tenant key causes `AccessDeniedException`. Also cloudtrail returned events for Encrypt and Decrypt except the decrypts at 02:12-02:18; S3 shows the CloudTrail object for that hour but the gz contains only management events, no KMS data events. Not sure how those would be missing."

Kai: CloudTrail can be configured to log management vs data plane events differently. KMS Decrypt shows up as an EventName=Decrypt (management event) and also includes `requestParameters.encryptionContext`. If the gz doesn't include these, maybe log delivery was truncated or a processing error occurred during the HSM failover window. We should request the raw gz file for 2028-12-02T02:00Z-03:00Z from their S3 bucket for us to inspect (we have access?).

Sara: Customer granted us read-only access to the audit bucket (bucket: s3://partner-audit-logs-210987654321). Asking them to upload the specific gz to a secure share if cross-account ACLs block listing.

Alex: Also confirm CloudTrail event selectors — if they had an old selector that filtered out KMS events (rare) or used CloudWatch Logs with a retention policy. If objects exist but KMS entries missing, AWS support will need to look at backend delivery during the HSM failover maintenance window. We should open a support case with AWS (flag as P2 / security-sensitive).

Maya: Action items: 1) Customer to run the local decrypt repro (done) and share exact CLI output (they did). 2) Customer to share raw CloudTrail gz for 02:00-03:00Z (requested). 3) Jamal/Alex will run policy/grant checks once we have role access into partner account. 4) I'll open an AWS support case if customer confirms CloudTrail objects present but missing KMS Decrypt entries.

Jamal: I'll try `aws cloudtrail get-event-selectors --trail-name customer-trail` once we have access, and also check S3 lifecycle policies around that prefix. If lifecycle archived/deep-archive happened inadvertently that could explain missing entries.

Sara: I'll update the customer with expected timeline — 24h to confirm policy/grants and 48h if we need AWS backend investigation.

Maya: Thanks everyone — I'll drop updates here when we have the gz file and AWS case number. :thumbsup:
